uncited: **Iterate over cells:** Loop through all grid cells.
*   Edge 0-1 (Bottom): Crossed if $(v_0 \ge L \text{ and } v_1 < L)$ or $(v_0 < L \text{ and } v_1 \ge L)$.
*   Edge 1-2 (Right): Crossed if $(v_1 \ge L \text{ and } v_2 < L)$ or $(v_1 < L \text{ and } v_2 \ge L)$.
*   Edge 2-3 (Top): Crossed if $(v_2 \ge L \text{ and } v_3 < L)$ or $(v_2 < L \text{ and } v_3 \ge L)$.
*   Edge 3-0 (Left): Crossed if $(v_3 \ge L \text{ and } v_0 < L)$ or $(v_3 < L \text{ and } v_0 \ge L)$.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot M)$, where $N$ and $M$ are the dimensions of the 2D grid.
*   **Memory Complexity:** $O(N \cdot M)$ to store the input grid.
The output size is proportional to the number of contour segments, which is typically much smaller than the grid size.
Marching Squares is the 2D analog of the Marching Cubes algorithm.
